ui.tagline: Find research questions nobody has answered yet.
ui.what_it_does: This tool reads a library of research papers and looks for gaps — questions a paper said needed studying that nobody followed up on, problems that several teams independently ran into, and methods from one line of work that might solve a problem in another.
ui.library_covers: how language models express confidence, when they should refuse to answer, how their uncertainty is measured, and why they state false things as fact
ui.library_summary: Right now the library holds 113 papers on how language models express confidence, when they should refuse to answer, how their uncertainty is measured, and why they state false things as fact.
ui.footer_scope: Working prototype · currently shown: 113 papers on language-model reliability. Not a comprehensive research tool.
ui.one_library_note: This tool searches one library at a time. Building a library means reading thousands of papers with an AI model — that costs real money and takes hours, so only this one exists so far.
ui.evidence_intro: Every result here comes from specific papers. These are the ones behind this one.
ui.findings_heading: How we checked our own work
ui.findings_intro: Where the method has limits, we wrote them down rather than smoothing them over.
ui.findings_are_technical: This is a working note written for the people building this tool, so it uses technical shorthand rather than the plain wording used everywhere else.

dev.on_note: Developer mode is on — showing raw scores, scorer internals, and pipeline provenance.

unfollowed_future_work.name: An unfollowed question
unfollowed_future_work.short: A question a paper said needed studying, that nothing else in this library followed up on
unfollowed_future_work.long: When researchers finish a paper they usually name the questions they could not get to. We collected those, then checked whether any later paper in this library actually went and did the work. These are the ones where nothing did.

unaddressed_limitation.name: A problem several teams hit
unaddressed_limitation.short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
unaddressed_limitation.long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.

method_transfer.name: A method that might transfer
method_transfer.short: A method from one area that might solve a problem in another
method_transfer.long: Two groups of papers that barely cite each other. One group has a method; the other reports a problem that method looks related to. Nobody appears to have tried connecting them — but we matched them by similarity, so this needs a human to check whether the connection is real.

disagreement.name: A disagreement between papers
disagreement.long: Two papers in this library that report findings pointing in opposite directions, where neither resolves the other.

corpus_relative.label: Only checked within these 113 papers
corpus_relative.text: Nothing in this library followed this up — but this library is 113 papers, not the whole field. Somebody outside it may well have answered this already. Check before you invest.

mixed_fidelity.label: Based partly on summaries only
mixed_fidelity.text: For some of these papers we only had the summary, not the full text. Papers we could read in full reveal far more about their own limits, so this may be built on an incomplete picture.

generic_category.label: Broadly worded
generic_category.text: The problem these papers describe is worded broadly enough that they may not be running into quite the same thing.

construct_gated.label: Narrow reading
construct_gated.text: This was matched on a specific technical reading of the topic, so related work phrased differently may have been missed.

semantic_lead.label: A promising match we haven't verified
semantic_lead.text: We matched these two papers because their wording is close, not because anyone confirmed the connection makes sense. It may not survive contact with an expert.

substantive.label: Checked — looks like a real connection
substantive.text: We went back over both papers and the method does appear to address the problem. That check was done by a language model reading the two papers, not by a specialist, so it raises the odds without settling them.

trivial.label: Checked — the connection is superficial
trivial.text: On re-reading, the two papers only look similar on the surface. Probably not worth pursuing.

not_addressing.label: Checked — the method doesn't address the problem
not_addressing.text: On re-reading, the method does not actually address the problem it was matched to.

unconfirmed.label: Not checked yet
unconfirmed.text: Nobody has re-read this pair to see whether the connection is real.

strength_meaning.Strong: Several independent papers point at this, and we could read their full text to check.
strength_meaning.Worth a look: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
strength_meaning.Unverified lead: This is a pattern we spotted automatically and have not verified. Treat it as a hint to investigate, not a finding.

abstract_only.label: Summary only
abstract_only.text: We only had this paper's summary, not the full text. Papers we can read in full tell us far more about what went wrong in them, so we know less about this one than the others.

full_text.label: Full text
full_text.text: We read this paper in full.

search.placeholder: What do you want to know about?
search.hint: Try: why do language models sound confident when they're wrong?

borderline.label: This is at the edge of what the library covers
borderline.note: We found some related work, but your question sits on the edge of this library's subject. The results below may be partial — and there may be plenty of good work on this that simply isn't here.

out_of_domain.label: That's not in this library
out_of_domain.note: We didn't find anything on that. Rather than show you weak matches dressed up as answers, here's the honest position: this library only covers {covers}.

no_results.label: Nothing matched
no_results.note: Your question looks like it's about this library's subject, but no specific result matched closely enough to show.

build_library.title: Building a new library
build_library.body: A library is built by collecting papers on a subject and reading each one with an AI model to pull out what it found, what didn't work, and what it said should be studied next. That is the expensive part.
estimates: about 100–150, the same size as this one
3–5 hours, mostly waiting on batch processing
the same search you just tried would work on that subject
build_library.not_yet: This panel is a preview, not a working button. Building a library isn't automated yet, and it spends real money, so it needs a human to start it. The estimates above are here so you know exactly what would happen and what it would cost — not so you can trigger it from this page. If you want a library built for a subject you care about, get in touch with the maintainer.

no_disagreements.headline: No disagreements found — and that is a real result.
no_disagreements.body: We checked every pair of papers that could plausibly disagree, and found none that actually contradict each other. This is not a bug or an empty database. The papers in this library largely agree with each other; they build on shared assumptions rather than arguing. As the library grows the number of pairs we check grows much faster than the number of real disagreements, which so far has stayed at zero.

attribution.label: Sources
attribution.intro: Paper metadata, citations and abstracts come from these openly licensed sources. Only short, structured extractions (claims, limitations, future-work statements) are shown here — full text was read to produce those extractions, not republished.
items: primary source of paper metadata, citations and abstracts (CC0)

libraries_note.label: Libraries in this project
libraries_note.intro: Each library is one subject read through the same pipeline. The library currently on screen is the one this URL renders; the others are on the same domain under /library/<slug>/.

items.name: Language-model reliability
items.note: The oldest, most-scored library in the project.

items.name: Diet and all-cause mortality
items.note: Research-literature analysis, not dietary or medical advice. The papers behind these results contradict each other on some of the most common questions (red meat, saturated fat, alcohol, low-carb). Take medical decisions to a clinician who knows you.

items.name: Algorithmic fairness in machine learning
items.note: Definitions of fairness are provably incompatible in general. Papers here disagree about which incompatibility matters for which decision.

privacy_note.label: Privacy
privacy_note.body: On the public deploy this page sends anonymised page-view counts to Vercel Web Analytics (which URLs got visited, roughly what country, no cookies, no cross-site tracking, no identifiers). What you type into the search box runs against an index in your browser — the query itself is not sent anywhere. Downloads (.bib, .csv) are generated locally. The local .app / .command versions and ?dev=1 opt out of analytics entirely.
